We design and develop simple yet powerful web and mobile applications. When pursuing work, we focus on interesting and meaningful projects. Over our 26 years as a company, we've worked with well-known technology organizations like Duolingo and Mozilla, not-for-profit organizations working in areas including </span><a href="https://blog.silverorange.com/usability-for-promotion-codes-and-access-codes"><span>affordable internet access for low-income families</span></a><span>, and with </span><a href="https://www.emrap.org/"><span>world-renowned doctors training other doctors</span></a><span> through online education.</span></div> <div>&nbsp;</div> <div><span>We’re proud of the fantastic products we’ve built in partnership with our clients and we’re actively invested in the processes behind these products. We are committed to fostering a team-focused approach in our work of building great user-focused systems, while also placing a serious emphasis on quality of life, openness, empathy, and a supportive work environment.</span></div> <h3><strong><span>The position</span></strong></h3> <div><span>We're looking for a full-time Director of Business Development to lead our efforts to expand our client base. For a long time silverorange successfully relied on word of mouth and existing partnerships to sustain our growth - we have now reached a point where we feel we need a dedicated business development specialist in order to meet our business goals. We’re looking for a strategic and proactive person who will leverage their expertise to shape our business development strategy and implement the processes to support sustained growth.&nbsp;</span></div> <div>&nbsp;</div> <div><span>This position is available immediately and we will work with you to get you started as soon as possible.</span></div> <h3><strong><span>Responsibilities</span></strong></h3> <ul> <li><span>Develop, maintain, and implement a strategic business development plan.&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span>Build out our sales pipeline; implement and maintain a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system or alternative for leads.</span></li> <li><span>Seek out, establish, and cultivate new client relationships.</span></li> <li><span>Act as the face of the company for events, client visits, business mixers etc.&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span>Seek and respond to appropriate requests for proposals; create proposals for potential new clients.</span></li> <li><span>Recommend a business-to-business marketing strategy while keeping an eye on industry trends, advise leadership of potential new markets and research to support our services.</span></li> <li><span>Maintain and/or coordinate open communication with existing and former clients to foster future work.</span></li> <li><span>Regularly report to the operations team on business development activities.</span></li> </ul> <h3><strong><span>Requirements</span></strong></h3> <ul> <li><span>Be eligible &amp; available to work from Canada.&nbsp;</span></li> <li><span>Be willing and able to travel nationally and internationally to meet with prospective clients.</span></li> <li><span>5+ years of experience leading business-to-business sales for an organization in the digital services industry.</span></li> <li><span>Experience developing, maintaining, and implementing a business development plan and actively managing a sales pipeline.</span></li> <li><span>Excellent organizational, verbal, and written communication skills. Experience working in a remote or asynchronous environment is an asset.</span></li> <li><span>Strong sense of ownership over and self-direction in the work.</span></li> <li><span>Strong client management skills.</span></li> </ul> <h3><strong><span>Growth &amp; ownership</span></strong></h3> <div><span>Our team is co-operative and will help you learn and expand your skills via mentoring, team-wide support, and learning opportunities. All members of the team are encouraged and given space to grow as individual contributors, and have ongoing opportunities in project and team leadership.</span></div> <div>&nbsp;</div> <div><span>We’re excited to hear your fresh ideas and approach. We have decades of collective experience, and we all continue to become better at what we do by both teaching and learning from each other. Add your voice to our mix!</span></div> <div>&nbsp;</div> <div><span>Opportunity for employee ownership is a fundamental part of silverorange (non-founders currently own more than a third of the company) and we’re currently working on new ways to transfer even more ownership to employees.</span></div> <h3><strong><span>Inclusion &amp; diversity</span></strong></h3> <div><span>People with different backgrounds and experiences make us stronger, and we’re always looking for ways to improve. Our team is getting more diverse across many dimensions of diversity, but we’re still missing perspectives that could make our work better. UI SDK is a library of UI behaviors from Vercel Labs that agents assemble into components. The README lists keyboard navigation, focus, selection, dismissal, popups, drag and drop, and the ARIA they need. All of it lives in @ui-sdk/core . Thin adapters render it in each framework. The project site explains the idea with a Select. You do not hand the agent a finished Select. You hand it a popup, a selection model and typeahead. Those same parts can produce an autocomplete, a combobox, or a component nobody has designed yet. How does UI SDK work? Components start as primitives defined with definePrimitive . A primitive declares state, an API and slots. Slots attach attributes, events and behaviors to DOM parts. The README example builds a search field with createFocusRecovery . Its Clear button appears only when there is text. Each framework then renders the primitive with createParts . The README says the parts are the same in all 5 adapters. So 1 behavior definition can serve a React app and a Svelte app. Which behaviors ship? Behaviors shown on ui-sdk.dev include: createRovingFocus : arrow keys move through a list with 1 Tab stop createTypeahead : type a few letters to jump to an item createPopup : opens next to its trigger and stays on screen createSelection : select 1 or many, with Shift and Ctrl createReorder , createResize , createViewport and createVirtualizer The docs group behaviors into 10 categories, from Focus and Keys to Canvas. Prebuilt components include Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Menu, Tree and Color Picker. How do agents learn it? Setup is a prompt you paste into your agent . It installs the packages and adds a note to AGENTS.md . That note points the agent to the ui-sdk skill and to llms.txt inside the package docs. The skill installs with npx skills add vercel-labs/ui --skill ui-sdk . Pages without a build step can load web.js and web.css from ui-sdk.dev, per the skill listing . Can agents operate the UI directly? Yes, the agent docs describe a bridge created with createAgent() before the page renders. agent.snapshot() lists components, their state and available actions. agent.act() runs an action, such as renaming a project with setValue . Apps can pass an allow callback to approve or refuse actions. Change callbacks receive source: "agent" and can cancel the change. Tools can also be registered with supported browsers through WebMCP. UI SDK benchmark: agent bridge vs browser tools Vercel compared its bridge against browser tools on 1 project-settings task. The agent renamed a project, updated members and notification settings, then saved. Both agents used Sonnet through Claude Code, with the same task and system prompt. Figures are medians of 3 runs .
